comment: Network fault signals for the RTX routers and WLX access points, turned into .es-query Kibana rules by setup-network-alerts.sh. Each signal becomes one rule named `Net: <title>`; the CT111 self-heal-observer turns an active alert into a self-heal-state doc, and self-heal-create opens a GitHub issue titled `[self-heal] Net: <title> :: query matched`. The rule NAME is therefore the issue title — put the diagnosis in it. Rules are tagged `netlog` and PRUNED when a signal is removed from this file, so renaming a signal retires its old rule instead of orphaning it.
_comment_why_these: Only signals that earned their place in a real investigation are here. `syslog_silent` is the highest-value one: in 2026-08 the wlx323 AP's syslog was silently discarded by Vector for weeks (~200k docs/day) because devices.tf and vector.toml declared the AP at .41 while it lived at .27 — ES showed zero docs and nothing alerted. That failure mode is invisible to every other rule, because every other rule reads the very stream that stopped. See home-monitor memory wlx323-wrong-ip-silent-syslog-drop.
_comment_absence_vs_presence: `comparator` `<` with `threshold` 1 = ABSENCE (nothing arrived — the stream died). `>` with 0 = PRESENCE (a fault signature appeared). Presence rules set `exclude_previous_hits` true so a one-shot event fires once and then recovers, which closes the GitHub issue on its own; absence rules leave it false because the condition is a standing state, not an event.
_comment_window: `window_minutes` must exceed the signal's natural quiet period or the rule flaps. syslog_silent uses 30 min because a healthy AP can be quiet for ~20 min at night (measured: wlx323 emitted 3 docs in the 5-min bucket at 02:21Z). Presence rules use 15-30 min so a burst is still inside the window when the rule next runs.

signals.title: syslog silent (wlx323)
signals.message: No syslog from wlx323 (192.168.1.6) for {{window}} min. Either the AP is down or the Vector pipeline is dropping it (check the source-IP map in cookbooks/lxc-monitoring/files/vector.toml against the AP's real IP, and vector_component_discarded_events_total on 192.168.1.76:9598).

signals.title: syslog silent (wlx402)
signals.message: No syslog from wlx402 (192.168.1.5) for {{window}} min. Same triage as wlx323.

signals.title: syslog silent (wlx313 ITM)
signals.message: No syslog from wlx313 (192.168.1.155, ITM). KNOWN GAP as of 2026-09: this AP has never shipped syslog, so the ITM site has no wireless visibility at all — the same class of blind spot that hid the wlx323 fault for weeks. Fix is to point its syslog at 192.168.1.76 and add its IP to the Vector source map; until then this issue stays open with self-heal-needs-human.

signals.title: syslog silent (RTX hnd)
signals.message: No syslog from RTX1210 hnd (192.168.1.253) for {{window}} min. This router normally emits 150k-290k docs/day, so silence is a hard signal.

signals.title: syslog silent (RTX itm)
signals.message: No syslog from RTX830 itm (192.168.1.254) for {{window}} min. Window is 3 h because this router only emits 100-300 docs/day; a shorter window flaps.

signals.title: wireless module restart (WLX)
signals.message: Wireless firmware subsystem restart (SSR) signature on a WLX AP. Between 2026-08-16 and 08-29 this dropped every SSID for 2-4 min, 30 times in 8 days, gated by an LLDP PD-monitor frame. Runbook: home-monitor docs/runbooks/wlx323-radio-stability.md. First check whether `lldp auto-setting use off` is still in the AP's running config — restoring a pre-2026-08-29 /ap_config backup from the RTX LAN map silently reintroduces the fault.

signals.title: Radio Optimization crash (WLX)
signals.message: The Radio Optimization daemon (`airlink optimization`, which auto-adjusts channel, bandwidth and transmit power daily at 03:00 JST) logged an internal error or restarted. First seen 2026-09-05T13:41Z, 11 min after the 5GHz(2)->6GHz(1) band swap; zero occurrences in the 189 h before that and zero on wlx402 ever.

signals.title: radio interface DOWN (WLX)
signals.message: A WLX radio interface went DOWN (<5121>). Confirm a matching <5120> UP followed for EVERY interface that went down — a DOWN with no UP means that radio never came back. Note the interface-level outage understates the client-visible one: on 2026-09-05 the interfaces were down 43 s but 5GHz clients could not associate for 109 s, because ACS landed on a W56 DFS channel and had to serve a 62 s CAC first.

signals.title: 5GHz stopped for DFS CAC (WLX)
signals.message: <0301> Started CAC — the SERVING 5GHz channel stopped transmitting for ~60 s. This is the DFS event that actually costs service. Deliberately NOT alerting on radar detection itself (<0303>/<6410>, 5 occurrences in the last 7 days) because Fast DFS v2 relocates in 0 s while it is active and the runbook concludes those need no action; alerting on them would file ~5 noise issues a week. <6404> is also excluded: that is the rolling CAC on the agile channel, not an outage. This matters more since 2026-09-05, when wlx323 lost its second 5GHz radio to 6GHz and has no other 5GHz to fall back to. Do NOT pin 5GHz(1) to W52 to avoid DFS: that stops Fast DFS v2 and the channel never returns from W52.

signals.title: DHCP error (RTX hnd)
signals.message: RTX hnd DHCP error. The scope is 192.168.1.20-99 (80 addresses, 12 h lease); the whole retained corpus has only ever contained Allocates/Extends/Released, so any of these tokens is new. Check `show status dhcp` for pool exhaustion.
